angle: the machine's own rule as a physical thing: what turning each knob would do to a real object
subject: A snow globe of silt: shaking it lifts a hatched cloud off the drift on its floor, and the cloud's lifted top edge is the one bright line.
controls: settle: position; how high the cloud's underside still hangs above the drift, resting on it at 0.1 s and floating about 0.4 of the globe higher at 10 s (thicker liquid).
layers: count; the cloud is hatched with exactly one 45-degree hairline per partial, so 2 layers is two strokes and 64 is a dense mass (spacing floors at 3.2 px, so it saturates near 40).
stir: shape; the cloud's top edge (the bright mutable outline) rises and bulges, highest in the middle, from a low skin at 0 to near the top of the glass at 100.
grain: scale; coarse flakes appear under the cloud and grow from nothing to about 10 px, and the top edge roughens.
reference: library/toro-blocks (solid vs hollow meaning different things; black fills behind outlines)
risks: A snow globe is a known toy and could tip toward novelty; it must stay drawn as an object (glass highlight, banded base), never as an icon.
Layers as hatch count saturates around 40 lines at the 3.2 px floor, so 48 and 64 look alike.
Settle shown as hang height is a snapshot of a time, not the rate.
